text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Greek side is calm in the face of Turkish threats and provocations to integrate the occupied areas to Turkey. Cyprus accuses Turkey of attempting to scupper the continuation of U.N.-sponsored talks on Cyprus next month.
- A Cypriot priest was viciously murdered by a woman in Athens yesterday morning.
- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash threatens to boycott the second round of talks on Cyprus in Switzerland.
- Turkey's declaration on the partial integration of the occupied areas was designed to force the Greek Cypriot side to quit the talks, but their plans were foiled, says the government.
- The dollar continued to surge against the Cyprus pound yesterday as economists predicted the Cyprus currency is ripe for a devaluation.
- Popular Bank opens its first representative office in the Balkans.
- The Cyprus Offshore Unit of Barclays Bank Plc commands a 24 percent market share in customer deposits.
- People who participated in the 1974 coup to overthrow Archbishop Makarios are now in line for promotions to the post of brigadier-general in the army.
- Turkey's threats to integrate northern Cyprus appear to have had no effect on the talks.
- Central abattoir remains shut for the fourth consecutive day amid disputes on new working hours.
- Woman is sought for the murder of a Cypriot archimandrite gunned down outside his Athens home yesterday.
